```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(easyNIS)
```

## Build the cohort design

`nis_design()` validates `YEAR`, `HOSP_NIS`, `NIS_STRATUM`, and `DISCWT`,
then constructs a survey design before applying the declared domain.

```{r design}
nis <- nis_open(nis_example(years = 2019:2020)) |>
  nis_flag_dx(heart_failure = "I50")
design <- nis_design(
  nis,
  cohort = heart_failure & AGE >= 18,
  keep = c(AGE, LOS),
  annualize = TRUE
)
srvyr::summarise(design, total = srvyr::survey_total(),
                 mean_los = srvyr::survey_mean(LOS))
```

The output contains a weighted fixture total and mean LOS with design-based
standard errors. Empty cohort hospital-years are retained as zero-domain
placeholder rows so domain variance uses the full sampled structure. This
placeholder strategy is experimental.

## Choose a pooling convention

Without annualization, pooled-year weights represent the combined included
period. `annualize = TRUE` divides by the number of valid years; partial years
count as a year. When quarter fields are present the function warns about
incomplete year coverage and a 2015 cohort restricted to one coding era.
Exclude partial years or choose a documented alternative if this convention
does not fit the estimand.

`nis_reweight()` multiplies the design weights by analyst-supplied weights. It
is experimental and does not replace the NIS discharge weight or the survey
design.

```{r reweight}
weighted <- nis_reweight(design, weights = rep(1, nrow(design$variables)))
srvyr::summarise(weighted, total = srvyr::survey_total())
```

With unit multipliers the result retains the original design-weighted total.
This is only a syntax example, not a recommended reweighting model.

## Why design-based standard errors matter

NIS uses hospital clusters, strata, and discharge weights. Ordinary means and
standard errors treat rows as if they came from a simple random sample and
do not reflect that structure. Use `srvyr` or `survey` methods on the returned
design for point estimates and uncertainty. A survey standard error is an
estimate of sampling variability under the supplied design, not a guarantee
that all sources of bias have been addressed.

## Inspect exclusions

Rows with missing, non-finite, or non-positive design fields are excluded
before the cohort is applied. Inspect the aggregate audit attribute and report
the exclusions with the analysis.

```{r exclusions}
attr(design, "nis_excluded")
```

This list gives counts by field and year, not record-level information.

## Common pitfalls

> **Common pitfalls**
>
> - Filtering the source data to the cohort before constructing the design
>   removes non-cohort sampled records.
> - Treating annualized weights as a correction for arbitrary partial-year
>   coverage.
> - Using non-survey summaries for estimates or uncertainty.
> - Treating reweighting or placeholder-row variance methods as established
>   methods; both are experimental.

See [`nis_design()`](../reference/nis_design.html),
[`nis_reweight()`](../reference/nis_reweight.html), and [Data notes by year](year-notes.html).
